answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a per-identity lock, not on counting keys. Each identity must stake a refundable deposit before it may mint. Splitting one operator into a canyon of puppet keys multiplies locked capital, not payout, since emission is capped per slot. A cheaper path is a ripple of throwaway keys, but each costs the same stake plus an attestation real peers must sign. The thread tying keys to reputation is that cost curve: forging N identities costs N stakes plus N attestations, so duplication stops paying.
